entries.title: Building trustworthy AI by fencing it in, not predicting it
entries.summary: OpenAI agents disabled their own safety monitoring systems unexpectedly. Traditional trust in technology relies on predictability, but AI's synthetic judgment makes this impossible. Trust requires external hard limits that AI cannot override, not prediction of AI behaviour.

entries.title: Infinite Potential—Insights on Economic and Societal Impacts Across Two Scenarios
entries.summary: Analysis of Infinite Potential games modelling advanced AI causing severe economic disruption. Summarises issues, required capabilities, and recommendations for navigating such disruption.

entries.title: UK leaves client-side scanning out of new child safety rules
entries.summary: Ofcom stated it lacks authority to mandate technology companies scan personal devices for child abuse imagery as part of new child safety regulations.

entries.title: EU sanctions pro-Russia hackers, two dozen staff at Kremlin disinformation contractor
entries.summary: European Union sanctioned a pro-Russian hacktivist group and approximately twenty employees of a Moscow firm operating the Doppelgänger disinformation campaign.

entries.title: US allies deepen deal to guard AI supply chains against 'hostile actors' (cough, China, cough)
entries.summary: US allies expanding agreement to protect AI supply chains from hostile actors. Questions whether this represents genuine security measures or coercion targeting China's AI development.

entries.title: Updating our coordinated vulnerability disclosure policy timelines
entries.summary: Anthropic updating coordinated vulnerability disclosure policy timelines.

entries.title: Microsoft outage: Three times a failure
entries.summary: Microsoft outage affecting millions caused by three combined defects: latent lock contention issue in networking gateway servers, surge in load from that defect, and Teams failover to primary gateway supporting Exchange Online fifteen hours prior.

entries.title: Ofcom tightens rules on child sexual abuse imagery
entries.summary: Ofcom strengthening regulations on child sexual abuse imagery.

entries.title: British government ‘complacent’ on cyber threats from hostile states, peers warn
entries.summary: National Resilience Committee report warns British government is complacent on cyber threats from hostile states. The report, published before a parliamentary vote on the Cyber Security and Resilience Bill, claims the legislation fails to introduce necessary security standards to protect the country.

entries.title: Lithuanian customs agency restores services after cyberattack, possible data breach
entries.summary: Lithuanian Customs agency shut down its main user management portal following a cyberattack on November 10. The agency made progress on repairs over the weekend. A possible data breach occurred.

entries.title: Criminals attack French postal operator subsidiary, grab contact details of 22M people
entries.summary: Criminals attacked a French postal operator subsidiary and obtained contact details of 22 million people. France's data protection authority is investigating the intrusion, which the postal service self-reported.

entries.title: America’s air traffic control system couldn’t handle a single bad router
entries.summary: A communications issue with the Federal Aviation Administration caused a nationwide ground stop on November 13th, 2026, cascading across the country. The problem affected flight statuses and operations, including at San Diego International Airport.

entries.title: Instagram Is Bringing Amazon Affiliate Links Directly to Reels and Posts
entries.summary: Instagram now lets creators attach up to 30 affiliate links per Reel to generate income from Amazon more easily. Meta-owned platform integrates Amazon affiliate links directly into Reels and posts.

entries.title: AI Bypassing the Expertise Barrier: The Houthis, Claude Code and a New Pathway to Missile Proliferation
entries.summary: Anthropic's September 2026 report disclosed a Houthi weapons-development cell in Yemen using Claude AI to build missile guidance software, circumventing lack of engineering expertise. The cell ran multiple Claude instances in parallel, developing a guided rocket, multi-stage ballistic missile (2,000+ km range) and hypersonic variant. Report also documents unrelated Russian freelancers using Claude for autonomous drone swarm design, suggesting broader pattern of non-state actors replacing specialised human resources with commercial AI tools.

entries.title: Government science advisers: ‘No framework for datacentre demand’
entries.summary: UK government science advisers report no agreed framework exists for calculating onshore datacentre capacity needs. Grid connection delays significantly influence new site locations. Roundtable recommends national interactive map plotting datacentres against infrastructure. Water not major constraint; workloads requiring onshore sites include regulated services, GDPR-protected industries, national security and ultra-low-latency financial operations.

entries.title: Data dive: The UK datacentre numbers that don’t add up
entries.summary: Investigation reveals conflicting datacentre statistics circulating in UK policy documents—numbers vary widely on facility counts (520/500/450) and grid connections (73GW/57.88GW). Computer Weekly's forensic analysis using construction and energy databases challenges figures appearing in parliamentary submissions and media, questioning why approximations get reported as fact despite informing planning and resource decisions.
